info.title: Nex Core host-local API
info.description: Development host-local HTTPS API v1, independent of Controller sessions and outages. Narrow appliance deployment and owned local power recovery; a local VM console WebSocket; no generic VM creation or network editor. Core outbound protocol and signed appliance format/protocol version 1 only. Deploy matching development components; no mixed-version upgrade window is promised.

servers.description: Selected Nex Core host; never the Controller API origin.

post.description: Authenticates only username root against the host operating-system password using PAM authentication and account checks, and validates browser origin. Use the root password set during Nex Core installation, or its current value after an OS password change. Locked or expired accounts/passwords and authentication-service failures fail closed, including the five-second helper timeout. Sets __Host-nex_local_session with Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path=/ and no Domain. Each login creates a new session; at most 64 active sessions per service. Sessions expire after 30 minutes without an authenticated mutation and eight hours absolutely; GET/HEAD polling does not renew them. Legacy unprefixed cookies are not accepted; sign in again after upgrade. The former separate local admin account and saved credential files are not accepted; there is no fallback. Upgrades require matching local service, PAM helper/configuration and web assets. Root password changes affect subsequent logins; existing sessions remain valid until logout, expiry or service restart. Controller admin credentials and Core protocol v1 are unchanged. Local process restart invalidates its in-memory sessions. Login admission permits at most five valid-length attempts per one-minute actual peer-IP window, two concurrent password checks per service, and 4096 tracked peers. Forwarded client-IP headers are ignored. Login returns 429 when rate/concurrency/table or 64-session capacity is exhausted; bounded retries must not create an unbounded loop.

400.description: HTTPS required, invalid JSON/input, password outside 1–1024 UTF-8 bytes or containing NUL; invalid password input is rejected before invoking the helper.

403.description: Origin must equal the request HTTPS origin; authenticated mutations also require the session CSRF token.

415.description: application/json required; request body limited to 32 KiB. Unknown fields and multiple JSON values are rejected with 400.

401.description: Authentication denied: wrong password, username other than root, locked or expired root account/password, or unavailable authentication helper. No local admin fallback.

429.description: Login admission permits at most five valid-length attempts per one-minute actual peer-IP window, two concurrent password checks per service, and 4096 tracked peers. Forwarded client-IP headers are ignored. Login returns 429 when rate/concurrency/table or 64-session capacity is exhausted; bounded retries must not create an unbounded loop. No Retry-After header is emitted because concurrency saturation has no fixed expiry.

get.summary: Show this Core's own pool membership
get.description: Authenticated local session. Read-only; safe to retry. Answers which pool this host belongs to, whether it is that pool's master or a member, the membership record it holds, and any staged join still in progress, from this host's own Core state. It exists so a host-local recovery procedure does not have to ask the Controller which pool a host is in: it works with the Controller unreachable or replaced, and it changes nothing. Every enrolled Core is a pool master until it joins another pool, so a single-host pool reports role master with one member row for itself.

200.description: This host's pool membership and staged-join status.

401.description: Missing or expired local administrator session.

409.description: This Core is not enrolled yet ("enroll this Core before reading its pool").

503.description: The membership record could not be read ("pool membership is unavailable"). Reported honestly as unavailable rather than as an empty pool; repair the Core state directory.

post.summary: Join this enrolled Core to a pool
post.description: Authenticated local root session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. This is the host-local recovery path; the ordinary workflow is the Controller's POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/members, which needs no CSR or offer handling by the operator. This Core must already be enrolled. It runs the same join precheck the Controller command path runs (enrolled, no managed VMs, no non-local storage, currently the master of its own single-host pool), validates the bare HTTPS master_url, pinned pool_ca_pem and opaque one-use offer, pauses its outbound agent, performs the Core-to-Core TLS 1.3 CSR exchange, then resumes reporting with the master-owned membership. The Controller may display/pass the offer but does not participate in peer authentication or keep membership intent. The local request body and offer are not echoed. A refusal before the exchange, a used or expired offer, an identity mismatch or a Core already belonging to another pool is 409 and leaves local membership unchanged; retry requires a new offer. Once the peer exchange succeeds the response is 200 and reports the stage reached in join, including stage rehomed with status needs_attention when this host is a member but its local resource rehome has not finished: Core retries the remaining stages itself. A 409 therefore means the host did not join; it never means an unfinished rehome. There is no cancellation after peer acceptance: reconcile membership inventory, or read GET /api/local/v1/pool, before retrying an interrupted browser reply.

400.description: Invalid JSON, master URL, pool CA or offer.

409.description: Core is not enrolled or the peer exchange was refused.

post.description: Authenticated enrolled local Core session and same Origin/CSRF boundary. Creates the private key in Core state and returns only host_id and CSR PEM. 409 if Core is not enrolled or CSR state cannot be prepared.

post.description: Authenticated selected-master local Core session and same Origin/CSRF boundary. Validates the member host/CSR and master HTTPS origin, then returns a 15-minute one-use offer bound to that CSR plus the pool CA. The Controller may relay this response but cannot redeem it. 409 if the Core is not a usable master or peer state cannot be persisted.

400.description: Malformed JSON or invalid member/CSR/master origin.

get.description: Authenticated local root session. Returns the Core-owned persisted clustered-storage operation projections. A 409 means this Core is not enrolled or its agent state cannot be opened. This read never creates a cluster, fence proof, mount or credential.

post.summary: Start Core-owned clustered GFS2 iSCSI setup locally
post.description: Authenticated enrolled local root session, same HTTPS Origin and X-CSRF-Token required. Starts the same Core-owned durable operation as the Controller relay; it is not a Controller job. Core forces its own pool and host scope, derives native mount/device data from verified iSCSI identity, and accepts no credential bytes or claimed fence proof. 202 means the Core accepted/reported the operation, not that a healthy cluster is ready. Same request ID with changed input conflicts in Core state.

409.description: Core is not enrolled or refuses the request.

get.description: Read-only libvirt inventory with ownership-based local power eligibility and refusal reason. Controller reachability does not grant ownership. An unavailable observation is an error, not an empty inventory or proof guests stopped.

post.description: Explicitly select the resident VM UUID. Only locally owned eligible appliances can be controlled; arbitrary guests and ambiguous ownership are refused. start, graceful shutdown and force-stop are supported. The client confirms the selected VM/action; no typed hostname is required and the legacy confirmation field is ignored. Persist a request_id before submission. Reusing the same ID/input observes the existing journal; interrupted or ambiguous effects are not automatically repeated. A 202 response is not proof of final power state: inspect the operation and fresh VM inventory. Controller outage neither stops guests nor permits takeover. Graceful shutdown returns stage shutdown_requested when the command is accepted; refresh VM inventory to establish actual shutdown. Power request journals are reconciled by resubmitting the same request; deployment polling routes do not expose power operations.

post.description: Persists one deployment intent before asynchronous work. Set a stable request_id, explicit configured local storage/bridge, resources, network_mode (static or dhcp), first Site and Controller password. Zero or omitted resource fields use 2 vCPUs, 4096 MiB and 32 GiB. Repeating identical normalized input returns the same operation; different input or a second deployment conflicts. The worker verifies the signed appliance, creates an independent disk and cloud-init seed, starts the original VM, verifies Controller TLS and completes enrollment/adoption. Poll the operation; guest boot is not completed handoff. Interrupted VM effects require observation and never recreate the appliance. DHCP waits up to five minutes at waiting_for_network for one usable IPv4 address from the guest agent on the exact owned VM/MAC; missing or ambiguous addresses produce needs_attention and can be retried. controller_url is absent until an address is found. The discovered IP is verified using the per-instance Controller certificate and hostname before handoff. DHCP requires matching rebuilt host and appliance components; omitted network_mode preserves static clients.

post.description: Explicitly retry the original persisted intent by its request ID without reposting the administrator password. Concurrent retries share the existing worker; a ready static operation remains unchanged, while DHCP rediscovery can refresh its address. VM effects reconcile the original journal and UUID instead of recreating or repeating an uncertain start; a deploy interrupted before its VM was defined (copying_disk or creating_seed), for which libvirt lists no domain with its UUID or name, removes its own partial files and restarts under the same UUID. Handoff can resume after Controller connectivity returns. DHCP retry and service startup rediscover the original VM address and verify its saved certificate/hostname; ready DHCP startup does this before resuming the existing enrolled agent. A changed lease with an active agent returns needs_attention requiring a local-service restart. This retains VM/host identities and does not require the original administrator password. Leases are not monitored periodically. A 202 response only accepts the retry; poll the original operation until ready or needs_attention.

post.summary: Push an enrollment token to this host
post.description: Lets the Controller enroll this host over its existing local session instead of the manual nex-core-agent enroll step. controller_url must be a bare HTTPS origin (no userinfo, path, query or fragment); ca_pem must contain at least one certificate; token must be 1-256 bytes with no control characters; replace_host, when set, is an existing revoked host id being replaced and must be at most 128 characters. server_name, when set, is the DNS hostname the Controller certificate is verified by and is kept with the identity for every later report; it must be a DNS hostname, not an IP address. Enrollment attempts on this host are serialized; a retried request queues rather than racing the embedded agent's on-disk identity. Already enrolled with a different replace_host returns 409 with the current host_id and changes nothing. On success the embedded agent persists its new identity, starts reporting to the Controller, and the response host_id also appears from GET /api/local/v1/host. The Controller's rejection of the token (expired, already used, wrong site) surfaces as 502 and leaves this host unenrolled; retrying with a fresh token is safe. The token and ca_pem are never logged or echoed back.

400.description: HTTPS required or invalid JSON/input: controller_url not a bare HTTPS origin, ca_pem has no certificate, token empty/too long/contains control characters, or replace_host too long.

get.summary: Open a local VM console WebSocket
get.description: Implemented in development product 0.1.0. WebSocket upgrade (RFC 6455, binary frames carrying raw RFB/VNC bytes for noVNC) authenticated by the local root session cookie; the Origin header must equal this host's HTTPS origin. The selected VM must be running on this host's system libvirt with a local UNIX-socket VNC display; any other display type is refused. The service bridges the browser to that socket directly and never opens a network VNC listener. This works without Nex Controller and is intended for guest installation and recovery from the host itself.

101.description: WebSocket established; binary frames relay the VM display stream.

200.description: Not returned; the stream is the 101 response.

400.description: HTTPS required or missing WebSocket upgrade headers.

401.description: Missing or expired local administrator session.

403.description: Origin must equal the request HTTPS origin.

409.description: VM is not running, not found, or has no local VNC socket display.

get.description: Refreshes the apt package index (at most every 5 minutes) and reports apt's candidate version for nex-core-local against the installed version. A package no configured source offers surfaces in error with HTTP 200. Root local session required.

post.description: Runs apt-get update then apt-get install --only-upgrade nex-core-local as root against the signed Nex archive, so dependencies resolve and the package signature is verified, then schedules systemctl restart via systemd-run --no-block. Fails if the installed version did not advance. Returns 202 scheduled on success. CSRF and same-origin required.

get.description: Authenticated local root session. Reads the complete catalog from the current pool master; local libvirt metadata is never substituted when master authority is unavailable. Works without Nex Controller.

post.summary: Create a stopped VM snapshot through Nex Core
post.description: Authenticated local root session; CSRF and same-origin required. Core validates exact VM ownership and stopped state, durably reserves the operation with the current pool master, records the native journal before effects, then performs and reports the operation independently of this HTTP connection or Controller. Reuse the same operation_id and exact request to retry; poll the operation route. A 202 acknowledges durable enqueue, not native completion.

202.description: Exact operation is durably accepted or replayed; poll for the outcome.

400.description: Invalid VM/operation ID or snapshot request.

409.description: Core is unenrolled, the operation ID was reused with different input, or conflicting work for this VM is unresolved. Native preflight refusals after durable acceptance are reported through the operation result.

503.description: Snapshot execution or current master authority is unavailable; reconcile the same operation ID before retrying.

get.description: Authenticated local root session. Reads the exact Core journal receipt by stable operation ID; pending/needs_attention remains unresolved and is not a success signal.

404.description: No matching local operation journal entry.

post.summary: Revert a stopped VM to a retained snapshot through Nex Core
post.description: Development slice under integration. Authenticated local root session, same-origin and CSRF required. Address the VM owner. The snapshot_id selects the retained point; operation_id is a distinct stable journal/retry identity. Core resolves captured state internally and binds the exact target to master authority. A 202 acknowledges durable enqueue, not completion. Follow the existing operation route; reuse the same identity and target after lost replies. No automatic VM start.

202.description: Exact operation is durably accepted or replayed; poll for the outcome.

400.description: Invalid VM, snapshot or operation ID, equal snapshot/operation IDs, or unsupported request fields.

409.description: Core is unenrolled, the operation ID was reused with different input, or conflicting work for this VM is unresolved. Native preflight refusals after durable acceptance are reported through the operation result.

404.description: Requested retained snapshot or operation is not found for this VM.

post.summary: Delete a stopped VM leaf snapshot through Nex Core
post.description: Development slice under integration. Authenticated local root session, same-origin and CSRF required. Address the VM owner. The snapshot_id selects a retained leaf point; operation_id is a distinct stable journal/retry identity. Core refuses points with native children before effects. Current leaf delete uses public blockcommit without --delete, metadata-only snapshot-delete, reference scan, and unlink of proven-unreferenced overlays. A 202 acknowledges durable enqueue, not completion. Follow the existing operation route; reuse the same identity and target after lost replies.

patch.description: Authenticated local root session, same-origin and CSRF required. Address the VM owner. Updates only the pool master's catalog name and description for an existing snapshot ID. Capture digests, creation time and disk identity stay fixed. Duplicate names and unresolved recovery reservations are refused. Later revert and delete bind the updated descriptor digest.

post.description: Authenticated local root session, same-origin and CSRF required. External NFS only in the current build. Persists the destination on the pool master. Core refuses same-ID source or observed filesystem identity replacement; register a new ID for a move and retain the old destination for old-point restores. A failed first NFS/SMB3 mount start cleans its new Core unit so a fresh operation can retry the same ID after service recovery; exact replay retains the failure.

Refuses (a failed Result, nothing changed) while a backup job uses it, an operation on it is running, a recovery point is in use by an unfinished restore, the name is wrong or the counts changed. Exact operation_id replay returns the recorded Result.

post.summary: Start a stopped full backup for a VM
post.description: Omitted or stopped requires a shut-off guest. crash is online crash-consistent push-mode backup. quiesced is refused until proven. UEFI online capture is refused in this development slice. Exact retry reuses the retained operation; changed input returns 409. For NFS and SMB3, uncertain final rename or sync remains needs_attention until exact point readback proves the result; pre-rename errors fail. In a capability-enabled SFTP or S3 repository, uncertain publication remains needs_attention until Core verifies the final point or safely aborts the exact incomplete upload. Controller only relays; Core owns publication.

consistency.description: Omitted or stopped for shut-off guests; crash for online crash-consistent; quiesced refused until proven.

409.description: Conflict with retained work or changed input.

post.description: Copies repository exports to local files before restore. Does not open NFS paths in place as VM disks. An SFTP point with a pending delete record is refused until the exact prune settles.

Core clears that request-only field before storage and inventory. Missing, zero or stale expected_revision on update conflicts. Exact operation-ID replay returns the retained outcome.

LocalSession.name: __Host-nex_local_session
LocalSession.description: Administrator session cookie __Host-nex_local_session, Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict, Path=/ with no Domain. Expires after 30 minutes without an authenticated mutation or eight hours absolutely. GET/HEAD polling does not extend idle lifetime; mutations also require matching Origin and X-CSRF-Token. At most 64 active sessions per service. Legacy unprefixed cookies are refused; sign in again after upgrading.

x-session-policy.idle_refresh: authenticated mutations after Origin/CSRF validation; GET and HEAD never extend it

status.description: Inspect status and error independently of progress. A running guest alone does not prove Controller handoff. needs_attention retains original identity and requires reconciliation. recovery_prepared is a manual CLI result only; it confirms an empty replacement awaiting explicit archive restore, not recovered Controller identity.

progress.description: Coarse workflow stage percentage, not measured bytes or estimated remaining time. ready at 100 indicates completed deployment handoff and seed cleanup. completed power operations acknowledge command completion; shutdown_requested does not prove the guest stopped.

controller_url.description: Controller HTTPS address when known. DHCP discovers an owned guest IPv4 address before publishing it; absence while waiting_for_network is expected. ready still requires verified handoff.

controller_cert_sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 fingerprint of the Controller leaf certificate DER. Verify this identity before trusting the new Controller browser certificate.

power_allowed.description: Local ownership eligibility; operations revalidate ownership and current observation before execution.

ready.description: Current host capacity, signed manifest and compatibility checks passed. This does not establish full image integrity or format safety; deployment verifies those before effects.

image_verification.description: Explains the verification boundary: preflight checks the signed manifest and compatibility metadata; full image SHA-256 and qcow2 safety checks run during deployment. Read blockers to determine whether manifest validation succeeded.

request_id.description: Persist before submitting. Stable identifier; replay must use identical normalized settings including original password.

cpus.description: Omitted or zero selects default; otherwise minimum 2.

memory_mib.description: Omitted or zero selects default; otherwise minimum 4096.

disk_gib.description: Omitted or zero selects default; otherwise minimum 32.

address_cidr.description: Static usable unicast IPv4 address with /8–/30 prefix; subnet and broadcast addresses are refused. Required for static mode; omitted in DHCP mode.

gateway.description: Another usable IPv4 address in the selected subnet, excluding subnet and broadcast addresses. Required for static mode; omitted in DHCP mode.

dns.description: One to three unicast IPv4 DNS server addresses. Required for static mode; omitted in DHCP mode.

admin_password.description: Initial Controller administrator secret: nonempty valid UTF-8, at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes, no CR, LF or NUL. No minimum length or complexity rule. Never included in operation responses. Retained privately only until handoff and seed cleanup complete.

site_name.description: Required nonblank name, maximum 200 UTF-8 bytes.

bridge.description: Explicitly select the configured existing management bridge. Deployment does not create or edit host networks.

storage_dir.description: Explicitly select the configured local storage directory returned by host preflight; this is not a pool/shared storage registration.

network_mode.description: Omitted or empty uses static for compatibility. The deployment UI defaults to DHCP. DHCP obtains IPv4 addressing, gateway and DNS from the selected bridge network. DHCP refuses nonempty static address, gateway or DNS fields.

then.description: DHCP accepts absent or empty static settings only.

expected_generation.description: Optional; zero is valid while Core allocates a candidate repository.

password.description: Current host root password, set initially during OS installation, 1–1024 UTF-8 bytes without NUL. Local web access does not set or reset the OS password.

request_id.description: Persist before submitting. Stable identifier; replay must use identical normalized settings including original password.

confirmation.description: Deprecated optional legacy field; ignored. Confirm the selected VM and action in the client before submission.

host_id.description: Enrolled agent host id, empty when not yet enrolled.

controller.description: Enrolled Controller HTTPS origin, empty when not yet enrolled.

request_id.description: Persist before submitting. Stable identifier; replay must use identical normalized settings including original password.

cpus.description: Omitted or zero selects default; otherwise minimum 2.

memory_mib.description: Omitted or zero selects default; otherwise minimum 4096.

disk_gib.description: Omitted or zero selects default; otherwise minimum 32.

address_cidr.description: Static usable unicast IPv4 address with /8–/30 prefix; subnet and broadcast addresses are refused. Required for static mode; omitted in DHCP mode.

gateway.description: Another usable IPv4 address in the selected subnet, excluding subnet and broadcast addresses. Required for static mode; omitted in DHCP mode.

dns.description: One to three unicast IPv4 DNS server addresses. Required for static mode; omitted in DHCP mode.

admin_password.description: Initial Controller administrator secret: nonempty valid UTF-8, at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes, no CR, LF or NUL. No minimum length or complexity rule. Never included in operation responses. Retained privately only until handoff and seed cleanup complete.

site_name.description: Must be absent or empty for replacement preparation.

bridge.description: Explicitly select the configured existing management bridge. Deployment does not create or edit host networks.

storage_dir.description: Explicitly select the configured local storage directory returned by host preflight; this is not a pool/shared storage registration.

network_mode.description: Omitted or empty uses static for compatibility. The deployment UI defaults to DHCP. DHCP obtains IPv4 addressing, gateway and DNS from the selected bridge network. DHCP refuses nonempty static address, gateway or DNS fields.

RecoveryPreparationRequest.description: Private 0600 JSON file consumed only by nex-core-local -prepare-recovery-file. Reuses deployment resource, network mode and password validation, but the Site name must be absent or empty: no handoff or enrollment is performed.

then.description: DHCP accepts absent or empty static settings only.

controller_url.description: Bare HTTPS origin of the Controller, no userinfo, path, query or fragment.

ca_pem.description: PEM containing at least one Controller CA certificate.

token.description: Single-use enrollment token minted by the Controller, 1-256 bytes with no control characters.

replace_host.description: Existing revoked host id being re-enrolled, at most 128 characters. Omit for a new host.

server_name.description: DNS hostname to verify the Controller certificate by when controller_url's host is not one of the certificate's names, for example the hostname of a Controller appliance deployed with DHCP. Must be a DNS hostname, never an IP address. Omit to verify by controller_url's host.

pool_ca_pem.description: Pinned pool CA PEM from the one-use offer.

peer_origin.description: Optional bare HTTPS peer origin advertised by this admitted member for durable master-side peer recovery.

join.description: The stage this host reached. 200 means the peer exchange succeeded and this host is a member; the stages after it are durable and retried by Core, so an unfinished rehome is reported here as stage rehomed with status needs_attention instead of a conflict that would wrongly tell the caller the join did not happen.

operation_id.description: Empty for a join started through this host-local route; set when a Controller pool-join command started it.

stage.description: The step still to perform; ready means every stage is done.

hostname.description: Host-reported name retained in the Core master membership and signed replica so a fresh Controller can name an offline member. At most 200 UTF-8 bytes of printable characters.

observed_at.description: When the master admitted this member, or created the pool for its founding host. Nothing rewrites it afterwards; the Controller reports it as joined_at.

peer_origin.description: Bare HTTPS origin this member advertised to the master for peer traffic. Recorded from the member's own advertisement, or, for the master's own row, from the master_url of the first Controller-driven join, which the master works out itself when none is supplied; never inferred from Controller connectivity.

system_uuid.description: This host's own SMBIOS system UUID, 32 lower-case hex digits without separators, reported by the host itself while it was alive: at join, and on every reconcile pass, so a pool formed before this existed gains it without re-joining. It is what proves a management controller belongs to this machine before it is powered off. Like peer_origin it is a recorded observation and moves no generation. A host too old to report one stays empty and simply cannot be given a BMC fence device.

replica_ack_excluded.description: Core-owned exclusion from snapshot reservation/settlement replica acknowledgements and ordinary replica-push failure aggregation, recorded only by a supported promotion after validating fresh exact fence evidence. Omitted means false. The host remains a pool member and VM owner; delivery is still attempted. The master clears the exclusion only after accepted current-membership VM inventory and an exact current-generation/content replica POST acknowledgement. Covered by the signed authority content, without changing membership generation when cleared. It does not exempt destructive resource-removal acknowledgements, storage-lease preparation, restart authority confirmation or future promotion fencing. Use matching development Core builds; old promotions are not retroactively excluded.

replica_generation.description: The master's observation of the authority-replica generation this member last acknowledged. Memory-only on the master and overlaid on the reported copy of the membership record: it is never written into the durable membership and is never an input to the generation equality rule. A member that has never acknowledged one is reported at 0, honestly.

replica_digest.description: Content digest the member acknowledged, as observed by the master.

replica_error.description: The master's bounded reason for the last failed push to this member: "pool member did not report its authority replica", "pool member did not acknowledge the authority replica", "pool member acknowledged the replica without joining the authority sanlock lockspace", "pool member acknowledged the replica without the Corosync key", "pool member refused the authority replica" or the member's own refusal text, "pool authority replica exceeds the peer body limit", or "pool member peer certificate cannot receive a wrapped pool CA key", "pool member did not report backup authority page progress", "pool member reported invalid backup authority page progress", "pool member refused backup authority page reuse", "pool member refused a backup authority page", or a refusal to report/stage a signed backup authority page.

replica_observed_at.description: When the master made that observation. Zero when it has none.

fence.description: How this host would be excluded from the pool if it had to be fenced: the same closed typed profile clustered storage already uses, recorded in the master's durable membership and replicated with it, so a promoted master inherits it and a fresh Controller re-adopts it. Only a virsh profile can be recorded by this build; Core refuses to record a profile it cannot verify. The credential reference it carries is never projected to a client, and neither is anything the reference names.

fence_credential_version.description: The master's counter for the private fence credential material behind this host's profile. The material itself is never in the membership; only this number is, so rotating it changes the replicated content and therefore advances the pool authority generation, while re-recording identical material moves nothing.

fence_readiness.description: The pool master's own answer to whether this host could be shut out, per method. Reported only by the master, only for the membership it owns, and never written into the durable record. Absent from a Core too old to report it, which a Controller shows as "not reported" and never as ready.

system_uuid_conflict_host_id.description: The member that already reported the hardware identity this host reports, when the master refused this host's report because of it. Without it the refusal is a dead end: an operator is told their host has no unique identity with nothing to act on. Cleared the moment the identity is accepted.

bmc.description: What this host's own Core found and did about its own management controller, reported to the master over the existing advertise peer route. It is an observation and a result, never a credential.

bmc_provisioning_disabled.description: The operator's own decision, recorded by the master, that this host must not configure its management controller for fencing. Clearing a fence device Nex Core provisioned sets it — one operator action with one meaning — and the host removes the account it created when it sees it. It is a decision, not an observation, so it lives with the fence profile in the replicated membership and a host cannot set or clear it by reporting about itself.

watchdog.description: This host's own watchdog capability, reported by the host and recorded by the master. A member too old to report one leaves it null, which is never counted.

watchdog_armed.description: That host's own report that it has armed its watchdog, recorded durably by the master. Null means the host never said, which is never a watchdog exclusion proof.

sanlock_host_id.description: Pool-master-assigned stable sanlock host ID. Zero or absent means this legacy member cannot participate in a storage lease.

sanlock_host_generation.description: Last native sanlock generation this host itself observed while its configured lease ID was live; not a proof by itself.

role.description: master when this host is its pool's master, including a single-host pool: that is a pool with one master and no members, never a host outside a pool.

members.description: This host's own membership record: the authoritative one on a master, and the copy validated at join on a member. Empty array, never null.

join.description: This host's durable staged join, or null when none is in progress.

restricted.description: This host's own refusal to act on pool authority, or null when it is acting normally. It is the answer to "why does nothing start here", which is exactly the question an operator at the host console asks when no Controller answers.

host_id.description: The host id this service is already enrolled as.

phase.description: idle, downloading, installing, restarting, done, or failed when an apply is tracked.

progress.description: Percent complete for the current apply when known.

error.description: Non-fatal repo or apply problem; installed_version remains valid for check.

kind.description: The structural form of reason, so no caller has to match on the sentence. unconfirmed is a master that has not re-proved its authority since it restarted; superseded is a host that found a higher authority elsewhere. Omitted by an older Core, in which case the sentence is the only signal.

reason.description: Why this host is refusing to act on pool authority.

conflicts.description: VMs this host still defines that the current pool master records as running elsewhere. A conflict is never resolved by guessing.

PoolRestrictedStatus.description: A Core-enforced refusal state on a host that cannot prove it holds the pool's current authority: while it is set the host writes no pool authority, mints no authority generation, starts no workload and autostarts nothing. Stop, power-off, console, local recovery access and reporting are untouched, and the libvirt hook refuses managed shared-VM starts by reading the host's own durable record, so the refusal holds with no Controller connected. It is reported by the authority probe, by inventory.managed.restricted and by GET /api/local/v1/pool.

username.description: Management-controller account for redfish and ipmilan, with power control only. It is not a secret and is reported back; its password is the credential. Absent on virsh and scsi_pr profiles, and a BMC profile without one can never produce a proof.

tls_fingerprint.description: Core captures the certificate the controller presents when the profile is recorded, keeps its leaf SHA-256 here and holds every later connection to exactly it: a factory management controller is self-signed with no usable name, so this pin, not a chain, identifies the endpoint the password is sent to and the power-off is issued through. A changed certificate refuses the fence with its own sentence rather than as a network fault. Reported so an operator can compare it with the controller's own page; it is not a secret and a client never supplies one. Absent on ipmilan, which authenticates its RMCP+ session and presents no certificate, and on virsh and scsi_pr.

virsh_uri.description: For virsh, exactly qemu:///system or qemu+ssh://<ssh_login>@<endpoint>[:<ssh_port>]/system. The latter must match the pinned SSH fields; it rejects passwords, query strings, fragments and every other URI path. An omitted URI port is valid only when ssh_port is 22.

cipher.description: The RMCP+ cipher suite an ipmilan fence must use, as the controller's own LAN channel offers it. Core selects it itself — 17 where the controller offers it, otherwise 3, the suite every IPMI 2.0 controller must implement — either while provisioning the account in-band or while proving a profile an operator entered. Suite 0 asks for no authentication, no integrity and no confidentiality, so it is never selected and never accepted here. Absent means none was recorded and ipmitool's own default is used. A client never supplies it; a request that does is refused with 400.

provisioned_by_core.description: The account behind this profile is one Nex Core created on the host's own management controller in-band. It is how a host knows, after a reboot or a master change, that the account under the Nex name is its own to replace rather than somebody else's to leave alone, and it is why an operator-entered profile is never overwritten by automatic provisioning. Written only by the pool master when the host's own Core reports the account it created; a client never supplies it, and a request that does is refused with 400.

StorageClusterFence.description: Closed Core fence profile. credential_ref and ssh_host_key_ref are opaque names for root-only Core secrets, never secret bytes; arbitrary commands and arguments are not accepted. Before any power-off Core asks the management controller which machine it manages — the Redfish ComputerSystem.UUID, compared exactly, or IPMI Get System GUID, where either documented byte order counts — and compares it with the target host's own SMBIOS system UUID in the master's membership record. A mismatch, a host with no unique hardware identity and an unreadable controller each refuse the fence and power nothing off. Redirects are never followed, so the identity cannot be read from one machine while another is powered off. A Redfish fence is performed by Core itself over the pinned connection — identity GET, ComputerSystem.Reset ForceOff, then a separate PowerState read — rather than by fence_redfish, which cannot be bound to the recorded certificate. virsh is for a Nex Core running as a virtual machine in a disposable lab and remains unaccepted for native production use.

host_id.description: The other host of the pair. A member reports it as the host it checked; the pool master reports it back as the host that did the checking, because the checks are listed on the row of the host they are about.

result.description: ok: the controller answered, accepted the recorded account and named this host's own machine. unreachable: it did not answer, or did not report the machine it manages. credentials_rejected: it refused the recorded account. identity_mismatch: it named a different machine, which is not a network fault and never a pass. certificate_changed: it presented a certificate other than the one the profile is pinned to. tool_missing: this Nex Core has no ipmitool. no_profile: no fence device is recorded for that host. unusable: the profile could never produce a proof, for example a host with no unique hardware identity.

detail.description: Core's own sentence for that result, shown verbatim. Never a credential.

power.description: The machine's power state as the controller reported it; absent when the controller did not say. Reported, never acted on.

profile.description: Binds this result to the fence device it was taken against: 16 hex characters over the profile's kind, address, target, account, pinned certificate and cipher, plus the hardware identity it is compared with. The pool master drops every result whose stamp is not the one its membership records now, so a replaced profile cannot inherit the checks taken against the one before it and reads as not checked yet until the next pass.

observed_at.description: When the pool master last had this result confirmed, on the master's own clock, so freshness never depends on two hosts agreeing about the time. Set by the master; a member does not send it.

stale.description: The master has not had this result confirmed for longer than it vouches for (three check intervals). A stale check is shown as stale and is never readiness.

PoolFenceCheck.description: One host's non-destructive read of another host's fence device: the management controller's own report of which machine it manages, and whether that machine is powered on, over the recorded profile and the replicated credential. Nothing on that path can power anything off. It is a Core observation and never enters the master's durable membership record.

checks.description: At most 64 results, one per host the caller looked at. An entry naming the caller itself is dropped: a host does not get to say whether it can be shut out.

PoolFenceCheckRequest.description: One checking pass, as a member sends it to its pool master.

ready.description: How many of this pool's ready hosts another host could shut out.

total.description: How many ready hosts this pool has. An ejected host is a tombstone in the membership, not one of this pool's hosts, and a host that has not finished joining is not one either; neither is counted.

unready.description: The ready hosts no other host could shut out, by host ID.

host_fencing.description: The pool's Host fencing setting as the master records it. It is on for a pool that has never been told otherwise. On by itself arms nothing: Nex Core arms a host's watchdog only where every prerequisite below holds.

prerequisites.description: Core's own checklist for arming watchdogs, computed on the master over the membership it owns. A client displays it and decides no line of it.

cluster.description: What this pool's own watchdog cluster is doing. Absent from a master too old to form one, which a client shows as no cluster line rather than as a cluster that is off.

PoolFenceSummary.description: The pool's own fencing answer, reported by the master with its membership: how many of this pool's hosts another host could shut out, which ones it could not, the Host fencing setting and Core's prerequisite checklist. A client displays it; it does not add up the rows it is about to render, which would count ejected tombstones and hosts that are still joining.

kind.description: The recorded fence profile's kind (ipmilan, redfish or virsh), or watchdog for the host's own self-fencing method. A host's row carries one entry per method.

state.description: ready: another ready host has a fresh successful check against this device. not_ready: Nex Core knows it would not work, and says why. unknown: Nex Core could not observe it, typically because nothing has checked this host yet. no_peer: this pool has no other host to be checked from, which is not a wait — a pool of one host also has nothing to promote over and needs no fence device. not_applicable: this pool cannot use this method at all, as a watchdog cannot be used below three hosts, and that is not something an operator can fix. Readiness is an observation shown to an operator: nothing here decides a promotion, which is decided by the live fence proof alone.

reason.description: Core's own sentence for a method that is not ready, shown verbatim. It names the host that found the problem, for example "this management controller did not answer (from host-b)".

checks.description: Every other ready host's last non-destructive read of this method against this host.

PoolFenceMethod.description: One way a host could be shut out, and whether it would work.

ready.description: At least one method is ready. No readiness at all, and readiness with no ready method, are both never treated as protected.

PoolFenceReadiness.description: The pool master's own per-method answer to whether this host could be shut out right now. It is derived from the membership the master owns and from the continuous non-destructive checks other hosts report, and is a memory-only observation overlaid on the membership copy the master reports, never part of the durable record. A master that has just restarted reports its methods as unknown until the next check pass rather than keeping a durable store of something one interval re-establishes.

state.description: What this host's own Nex Core found on its own management controller. provisioned: Core created its fence account and the master recorded the profile. no_local_interface: no /dev/ipmi0, so there is nothing to configure from the inside. user_management_refused: the controller refused in-band account management, or has no free user slot. lan_disabled: the controller reports no LAN address on any channel, or offers no authenticated RMCP+ cipher suite. name_conflict: an account under the Nex name exists that Core did not create, and nothing was changed. manual_profile: an operator entered a profile, which always wins. removed: an operator removed the account and automatic provisioning stays off for this host. pending_master: the account exists but the master has not recorded the profile yet, so this host has no usable fence device and is never shown as having one.

detail.description: Core's own sentence for that state, shown verbatim. Never a credential.

address.description: The controller's own LAN address as it reports it in-band.

channel.description: The controller's LAN channel the account was created on.

account.description: The account name Core created; not a secret. Its password goes to the master's private fence-credential store and nowhere else.

observed_at.description: When this finding last *changed*, not when it was last confirmed. An unchanged finding is deliberately not re-reported: the membership is signed and replicated, so a moving timestamp would re-sign and re-push the pool's whole authority every reconcile pass. It therefore says nothing about whether the host is still reporting. Liveness is that host's own connection, and the freshness of a fence device is PoolFenceCheck.observed_at, which the pool master stamps on its own clock every time a check is confirmed.

PoolHostBMC.description: One host's own report about its own management controller, kept in the pool master's membership record. It is a Core observation: a fresh Controller recovers it with the rest of the membership and stores nothing of its own. A member too old to report one is absent.

kind.description: Only a device that resets the machine independently of the kernel can count: hardware, and emulated where the host is itself a virtual machine and the hypervisor really does reset it. The kernel's softdog is software — a hung kernel does not run it — so it is reported and reported as not counting. A driver Nex Core does not recognise is unknown and counts as nothing until it is classified.

device.description: The sysfs device name, for example watchdog0. Not a path under /dev: Nex Core never opens the device node, because on most drivers opening it arms the timer.

driver.description: The kernel driver behind the device, which is what the classification is made on.

timeout_seconds.description: The device's configured timeout. Zero means the kernel did not say.

nowayout.description: The kernel's setting that closing the device does not stop the timer. Where it is set, Nex Core cannot disarm this host without rebooting it, and reports that rather than resetting the host to get out of it.

in_use.description: Something already holds the device open, read from sysfs rather than by opening it.

PoolHostWatchdog.description: One host's own report of the watchdog device it has, read from sysfs on the host it is about and recorded by the pool master. A watchdog is how a host shuts itself out, so it has to have been reported while the host was alive. It is a slow-changing capability: it is written only when the finding changes and carries no timestamp, because nothing decides anything from how long ago a host last said it.

name.description: Which line of the checklist this is: enough hosts for a majority side, a hardware watchdog on every host, a confirmed fence device on every host, and the pool's quorum.

state.description: unknown is Nex Core saying it cannot observe this yet and is never read as met. Quorum is unknown until this pool runs a quorum service.

detail.description: Core's own sentence for this line, shown verbatim, naming the hosts a line is unmet for.

hosts.description: Which hosts the sentence is about, as host IDs. Nex Core ends detail before naming them and puts them here, because only a client knows their display names.

PoolFencePrerequisite.description: One line of the prerequisite checklist Nex Core reports for arming watchdogs.

armed.description: Whether this host is feeding a watchdog that will reset it if it stops. A host that is not armed says why in detail.

kind.description: The device class this host armed. emulated is a device a hypervisor presents to a host that is itself a virtual machine: it really does reset that machine, so Nex Core arms it, and every proof and row resting on one says so because a hypervisor reset is not evidence about hardware. A physical host never reports it.

device.description: The sysfs device name sbd was given.

timeout_seconds.description: How long after sbd stops feeding the device this host resets. A watchdog exclusion proof needs at least twice this.

fencing_generation.description: The pool membership generation this host armed at. A watchdog exclusion proof is refused unless this is the generation being promoted, so a host that armed under an earlier record of the pool cannot be shut out on the strength of it.

detail.description: Nex Core's own sentence for why this host is not armed, or why it could not be disarmed cleanly.

feeding.description: Whether this host's watchdog device is still being fed, which is not the same question as armed. armed is what the pool may rest a proof on and goes false the moment the pool decides this host should stop; the device itself is released only when that host's cluster next stops, which can be a pass or two later. Every other host needs the difference: a host that leaves the pool's cluster while a peer is still feeding can take that peer below quorum, and that peer resets with nothing wrong.

observed_at.description: When this finding last changed, in the manner of PoolHostBMC.observed_at — not when it was last confirmed. Nothing decides anything from it: staleness is fencing_generation, which is durable and replicated and therefore still readable by a candidate whose master has gone.

armed_at.description: The host's own clock when it started feeding this device, carried over unchanged while it goes on feeding the same one. Nothing compares it with another host's clock. It exists so that a host which stopped and started its watchdog — a reboot, a cluster restart — produces a record that differs from the one before it: an identical record is never written and never replicated, and a survivor would otherwise be unable to tell "armed since before it left" from "was armed once, and has been up unarmed since". A survivor refuses a watchdog proof against a target that rejoined its Corosync partition after the last armed record it holds.

PoolWatchdogArmed.description: A host's own report that it has armed its watchdog, kept in the pool master's durable membership and replicated. It is the first of the three conditions of a watchdog exclusion proof, and the host that has to read it is a promotion candidate whose master has gone, which is why it is durable rather than an observation.

PoolFenceCluster.description: The pool master's memory-only Corosync/Pacemaker cluster observation. Pools of three to five ready hosts may arm diskless sbd; an eligible two-host pool may instead report a connected and voting qdevice witness while watchdog arming stays withheld. The selected witness and host armed reports remain durable on Core, not in this derived status.

state.description: off is the pool's Host fencing setting; not_available means no applicable cluster. In a two-host pool, forming means qdevice or native quorum is not verified and can coexist with an operating witness; degraded means witness and quorum are operating but watchdogs remain unarmed. Larger pools use forming for Corosync quorum, arming for rollout and degraded when hosts are not all armed.

detail.description: Core's own sentence for the state. A client shows it as written.

witness.description: The pool master's current native qdevice observation, separate from watchdog arming. Omitted when no witness is selected.

armed.description: How many hosts of this pool's cluster are feeding a watchdog.

total.description: How many hosts are in this pool's cluster. Every ready host that is not in maintenance is in it: a host is never silently left out of the quorum the rest of the pool makes its decisions with.

arming_host_id.description: The host whose turn it is to arm, by host ID. Arming means restarting that host's cluster services, so exactly one host in a pool does it at a time, and whose turn it is is derived from the membership rather than granted. A host that cannot arm holds the turn and the rollout stops there with that host's own reason, which is the safe direction: fewer armed hosts is less protection, never a false proof.

PoolVMSnapshot.description: Compact master-owned snapshot descriptor. Disk paths, XML and native artifacts remain in the owning Core journal.

mode.description: Create capture mode. Omitted or stopped requires a shut-off guest. crash and quiesced require a running guest; quiesced also requires a responding guest agent. UEFI running capture is refused in this development slice.

PoolVMSnapshotDependencies.description: Sorted resource IDs referenced by the captured VM definition. Omitted on legacy descriptors when the historical dependencies are unknown.

PoolVMSnapshotRevertRequest.description: New operation identity, distinct from the retained snapshot ID in the route. VM specification, descriptor and native paths are resolved by Core and cannot be supplied by the caller.

PoolVMSnapshotDeleteRequest.description: New operation identity, distinct from the retained leaf snapshot ID in the route. Target descriptor and native paths are resolved by Core and cannot be supplied by the caller.

PoolVMSnapshotMetadataRequest.description: Name is required; description is optional. Empty description clears the stored note. Capture digests and disk identity stay fixed.

BackupRepository.description: Master-owned backup destination record. Kinds are NFS, SMB3, S3 and SFTP; Core validates the kind and source.

source.description: Legacy NFS source; emitted for NFS records and omitted for other destination kinds.

credential_ref.description: Opaque Core-owned credential receipt reference; never credential material.

BackupRecoveryPoint.description: Master catalog index for one completed recovery point.

policy_id.description: Policy that created the point; retention prunes only that policy's points. Empty for manual backups.

BackupRun.description: Master-owned backup or restore run record.

capture_mode.description: Scheduled or run-now capture mode when present.

retention.description: Retention attached to a scheduled or run-now run when present.

host_id.description: Owner host of the backup or restore run when assigned.

manifest_sha256.description: Master catalog manifest digest pinned in a new restore run. Optional only for readable legacy runs; an unbound restore cannot execute or replay.

expected_revision.description: Request-only compare-and-set value for a policy update. It must equal the current durable revision; Core removes it before persisting or reporting the policy.

BackupDiskArtifact.description: One complete standalone disk image in a recovery point.

BackupFirmwareArtifact.description: Captured firmware payload relative to the recovery point.

BackupNowRequest.description: Starts a full backup of one VM into a registered repository.

policy_id.description: Creating policy, set by the scheduler; empty for manual backups.

RestoreAsNewRequest.description: Restores a recovery point as a new stopped VM from local copies.

host_id.description: Selected executing host; Core checks pool ownership.

RestoreReplaceRequest.description: Restores a recovery point over an existing VM identity with exclusive cutover.

host_id.description: Selected executing host; Core checks pool ownership.

ProtectRecoveryPointRequest.description: Sets or clears deletion protection on a catalog recovery point.

TestRestoreRequest.description: Restores as a new VM marked for verification and later cleanup.

host_id.description: Selected executing host; Core checks pool ownership.

TestRestoreVerifyRequest.description: Records the operator verification result for a test restore.

TestRestoreCleanupRequest.description: Removes only the selected test VM and staging for that test.

CatalogImportRequest.description: Scans one repository and imports validated manifests into the catalog.

BackupRestorePin.description: Prevents prune while a restore uses the recovery point.

BackupScheduleRule.description: One local-time cadence for a policy schedule.

BackupRetention.description: Keeps successful points per VM; age protection is optional.

BackupPolicyLimits.description: Optional advanced throughput bounds for a backup policy.

BackupPolicyVMOverride.description: Adjusts retention or capture for one VM in a policy.

BackupPolicyRef.description: Compact committed policy/schedule reference for takeover.

BackupRunRef.description: Compact committed or unresolved run reference for takeover.

PoolBackupAuthority.description: Bounded replica section for backup repositories, policy/schedule definitions, retained runs and catalog index. Full NFS recovery-point payloads are never embedded.

repositories.description: Durable NFS backup destination registrations for master takeover.

definitions.description: Full committed policy/schedule definitions for master takeover.

history.description: Retained and unresolved backup/restore run records for master takeover.

catalog.description: Master catalog index entries only; NFS payloads are never embedded.

policies.description: Compact policy refs derived from definitions for observation.

runs.description: Compact run refs derived from history for observation.

pins.description: Active restore pins transferred to the new master before retention can prune.

metadata_receipts.description: Durable operation result receipts retained for exact metadata retry after master takeover.

BackupMetadataReceipt.description: Durable outcome of one Core-owned backup metadata mutation, retained for exact replay after master promotion.

state.description: Operating means the pool master verified the selected qdevice's identity, pinned CA, TLS connection and cast vote. It does not imply an armed watchdog or an automatic fence proof.

detail.description: Core's current native observation or reason the witness is still forming.

BackupS3Source.description: Backup BackupS3Source contract. Planned until the corresponding Core capability is advertised.

endpoint.description: HTTPS endpoint with verified TLS identity.

BackupSFTPSource.description: Backup BackupSFTPSource contract. Planned until the corresponding Core capability is advertised.

OrphanCleanupRequest.description: Deletes the recovery points of the chosen VMs, which are not in the pool's VM inventory, from a repository's destination and catalog.

vm_ids.description: VMs chosen explicitly; there is no wildcard.

include_protected.description: Also delete protected points; otherwise they are skipped.

confirmation.description: 'delete N recovery points', or 'delete N recovery points including P protected' with include_protected.

recovery_points.description: Recovery points of the chosen VMs the operator was shown.

protected_points.description: How many of them are protected.

BackupOrphanGroup.description: One missing VM's recovery points in a repository.

vm_name.description: Name recorded by the newest point.

size_bytes.description: Sum of the sized points' disk and firmware artifacts.

size_unknown_points.description: Points the destination could not size within the query's budget.

in_use.description: A point is pinned by an unfinished restore or test restore, or a pending backup run names the VM; cleanup skips those points.

BackupOrphanQuery.description: A repository's recovery points whose VM id is not in the pool master's durable VM inventory.

warnings.description: Backup jobs that still list a VM missing from the pool.

BackupOrphanCleanup.description: The pool master's durable record of one orphaned-backup cleanup: the planned points and each one's outcome.

nex-core-local -prepare-recovery-file.description: Root-only manual replacement preparation, not an HTTP operation or running listener. Requires stopped local service and a clean replacement host without outbound agent identity or normal deployments. Uses the selected signed appliance and existing local storage/bridge. Does not bootstrap a Site, enroll a host or adopt the VM. Repeated identical normalized file contents reconcile the persisted request and original VM UUID; changed contents fail. TLS-verified readiness and seed removal precede recovery_prepared.

inputFile.validation: One JSON object in a regular file; unknown fields rejected.

output.format: One JSON object on stdout after successful completion.

nex-core-local -prepare-recovery-file.failure: Nonzero exit and error on stderr. Retain original request and journal; inspect uncertain VM effects before retry. No automatic restore, takeover or enrollment.
nex-core-local -prepare-recovery-file.compatibility: Same signed appliance format/protocol v1 and architecture amd64 as ordinary deployment. Restore requires matching source SHA-256 via the separate manual recovery command.

backup-test-verify.semantics: Controller queues operator verification of a test restore. Core records the result beside the catalog point; Controller adopts from master inventory.

backup-test-cleanup.semantics: Controller queues cleanup of one test restore VM and its staging only. Core removes that test guest; other recovery points are untouched.

backup-policy-upsert.semantics: Controller queues create/update of a master-owned backup policy. Core persists pool-backup-policies.json; exact request_id replay is required.

backup-policy-pause.semantics: Controller queues pause or resume of a backup policy on the pool master. Core owns enabled/paused state; Controller adopts inventory.

backup-policy-run-now.semantics: Controller queues an immediate one-shot run of a backup policy for selected VMs. Core records occurrence IDs under pool-backup-runs/; Controller adopts outcomes.
